slides.title: Introduction to Deployment
slides.content:
# Model Deployment 🚀

Take your model from notebook to production!

## What you'll learn:
- **Model Serialization** - Saving and loading models
- **APIs** - Serving predictions
- **Cloud Deployment** - Hosting on cloud platforms

## Why Deployment Matters

```
Jupyter Notebook → Only you can use it
        ↓
Deployed API → Anyone can get predictions!
```

## Deployment Pipeline

```
1. Train model → 2. Save model → 3. Create API → 4. Deploy → 5. Monitor
```

> 💡 **85% of ML projects never make it to production** - don't be one of them!

slides.title: Model Serialization
slides.content:
# Saving and Loading Models 💾

## Joblib (Recommended for sklearn)

```python
import joblib

# Save model
model = RandomForestClassifier()
model.fit(X_train, y_train)
joblib.dump(model, 'model.joblib')

# Load model
loaded_model = joblib.load('model.joblib')
predictions = loaded_model.predict(X_new)
```

## Pickle (Built-in Python)

```python
import pickle

# Save
with open('model.pkl', 'wb') as f:
    pickle.dump(model, f)

# Load
with open('model.pkl', 'rb') as f:
    model = pickle.load(f)
```

## Saving TensorFlow/Keras Models

```python
# Save entire model
model.save('my_model.h5')
# or
model.save('my_model')  # SavedModel format

# Load
loaded = tf.keras.models.load_model('my_model.h5')
```

## PyTorch Models

```python
# Save state dict (recommended)
torch.save(model.state_dict(), 'model.pth')

# Load
model = MyModel()
model.load_state_dict(torch.load('model.pth'))
model.eval()
```

> 💡 **Joblib is faster than Pickle** for large numpy arrays!

slides.title: Creating APIs with FastAPI
slides.content:
# Serving Models with FastAPI 🔌

## Simple Prediction API

```python
# app.py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic import BaseModel
import joblib
import numpy as np

app = FastAPI()

# Load model once at startup
model = joblib.load('model.joblib')

class PredictionInput(BaseModel):
    feature1: float
    feature2: float
    feature3: float

class PredictionOutput(BaseModel):
    prediction: int
    probability: float

@app.post('/predict', response_model=PredictionOutput)
async def predict(data: PredictionInput):
    features = np.array([[data.feature1, data.feature2, data.feature3]])
    prediction = model.predict(features)[0]
    probability = model.predict_proba(features)[0].max()
    
    return PredictionOutput(
        prediction=int(prediction),
        probability=float(probability)
    )
```

## Running the API

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn
uvicorn app:app --reload

# API available at http://localhost:8000
# Docs at http://localhost:8000/docs
```

## Making Requests

```python
import requests

response = requests.post(
    'http://localhost:8000/predict',
    json={'feature1': 5.1, 'feature2': 3.5, 'feature3': 1.4}
)
print(response.json())
# {'prediction': 0, 'probability': 0.95}
```

slides.title: Cloud Deployment
slides.content:
# Deploying to the Cloud ☁️

## Docker Container

```dockerfile
# Dockerfile
FROM python:3.9-slim

WORKDIR /app
COPY requirements.txt .
RUN pip install -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

CMD ["uvicorn", "app:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]
```

```bash
# Build and run
docker build -t ml-api .
docker run -p 8000:8000 ml-api
```

## Cloud Platforms

| Platform | Best For |
|----------|----------|
| **AWS SageMaker** | Full ML lifecycle |
| **Google Cloud AI** | AutoML, easy scaling |
| **Azure ML** | Enterprise integration |
| **Heroku** | Simple, quick deploys |
| **Railway/Render** | Modern, easy CI/CD |

## MLflow for ML Lifecycle

```python
import mlflow

# Track experiments
with mlflow.start_run():
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    mlflow.log_param('n_estimators', 100)
    mlflow.log_metric('accuracy', 0.95)
    mlflow.sklearn.log_model(model, 'model')

# Deploy registered model
mlflow models serve -m "models:/my_model/1" --port 5001
```

> 🎯 **Docker ensures your model runs the same everywhere!**

slides.title: Best Practices
slides.content:
# Deployment Best Practices 📋

## Model Versioning

```python
import joblib
from datetime import datetime

# Version your models
version = datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')
joblib.dump(model, f'model_v{version}.joblib')
```

## Input Validation

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, validator

class PredictionInput(BaseModel):
    age: int
    income: float
    
    @validator('age')
    def validate_age(cls, v):
        if v < 0 or v > 150:
            raise ValueError('Invalid age')
        return v
```

## Monitoring

```python
import logging
import time

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

@app.post('/predict')
async def predict(data: PredictionInput):
    start = time.time()
    
    prediction = model.predict([data.features])[0]
    
    duration = time.time() - start
    logger.info(f"Prediction: {prediction}, Time: {duration:.3f}s")
    
    return {'prediction': prediction}
```

## Health Check Endpoint

```python
@app.get('/health')
async def health():
    return {'status': 'healthy', 'model_loaded': model is not None}
```

> 💡 **Always log predictions for debugging and monitoring!**

## Quick Deployment Template

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
import joblib

app = FastAPI()
model = joblib.load('model.joblib')

@app.post('/predict')
async def predict(data: dict):
    return {'prediction': model.predict([data['features']])[0]}
```

> 🎯 **You now know the full ML pipeline from data to deployment!**
